text:
maria: Quick follow-up to the lazy-reservation experiment thread. I want to capture an implementation-first plan for ALLOC_LAZY as a wrapper (min surface change) and list the failure modes we need to cover. tagging @alex @tomas for perf/impl notes.

alex: TL;DR: wrapper is good. We add a per-alloc flag ALLOC_LAZY; allocator returns same handle but marks pages with a \"reserved_hint\" bit and updates a tenant-ledger. Actual physical pages are only materialized on first fault/commit.

tomas: important: we cannot let reserved-only bookkeeping affect eviction/admission incorrectly. Split budgets: light_reserve_budget (cheap, small) vs resident_quota. Evictor should only treat resident_quota when making admission decisions.

jin: NUMA + offload note: when a reserved range later commits, we must ensure we can satisfy NUMA affinity. If the host has already offloaded neighboring pages, commit path should support selecting preferred NUMA or fallback. Async commit helps.

lisa: measurement: small tensors microbench (seq=1024, batch=16 short-lived) showed ~22% less virtual fragmentation when we delayed backing for 8-16ms. But 99.9p commit latency can be 7-12ms if we end up doing blocking memcpy from remote backing. That's actionable with hedging.

maria: hedging proposal: default behavior async_commit+deadline_ms. on first access: spawn async memcpy/prefetch; resume execution if compute can tolerate missing cache-lines; if deadline misses, fallback to blocking_commit. expose commit_hedge_mode enum: {none, async_fallback, prefault_always}.

alex: code sketch for hedging (pseudo):```c
if (alloc.flags & ALLOC_LAZY) {
  if (page_fault) {
    if (cfg.hedge == ASYNC_FALLBACK && async_supported) {
      start_async_commit(page);
      return CONTINUE_EXEC;
    }
    blocking_commit(page);
  }
}
```

sre-jen: operational requirements: TTL on lightweight reservations (default 200ms), guaranteed cleanup on process exit, and a periodic GC that reclaims stale reservations. Alerting: reserved_never_committed_ratio > 0.1 for 1h -> pager. Also track reserved-resident delta per-host to detect leak patterns.

raj: product knobs: per-tenant max_light_reserve_bytes, reserved_timeout_ms, commit_hedge_mode. Add console metrics: reserved_count, reserve_to_commit_ratio, avg_commit_latency, 99.9p_commit_latency. Also allow per-route override so customers can opt-in for latency sensitive routes.

jin: offloader behavior: offloader must be able to evict physical pages that correspond to RESERVED hints without releasing reservation tokens. Eviction priority: PINNED > RECENT_COMMITTED > RESERVED_HINT. When evictor frees resident mapping of a RESERVED page, it must leave page meta indicating still_reserved so commit still allowed.

maria: meta design: add page_meta flags: \"reserved_hint\" and \"reserved_ts\". Reserve ledger per-tenant holds soft bytes and hard_limit. Compactor should consider reserved_hint as virtual fragmentation weight; reserved_age influences compaction priority.

tomas: impl detail: to avoid ABI churn we implement allocator wrapper inside runtime: callers pass ALLOC_LAZY flag; the runtime returns same pointer/handle. Under the hood we maintain shadow mappings that respond to faults. This avoids changing user-facing SDKs.

alex: perf numbers from my sim-run: eager baseline per-small-tensor alloc+commit = 5.1ms. ALLOC_LAZY reserved fastpath = 0.7ms. async commit average = 1.0ms; blocking tail = 9.7ms. For short-lived lifetimes (<30ms) we net positive. Need to restrict for long-lived allocations.

lisa: suggestion: auto-tune heuristic that disables ALLOC_LAZY for allocation sizes or routes where commit tail costs outweigh savings. Use quick telemetry bucket: if reserve_to_commit_ratio < 0.25 or average lifetime > 100ms revert to eager for that route.

sre-jen: failure cases: worker crash while reservations outstanding -> on restart, tenant ledger should subtract outstanding reserved bytes; make reservations ephemeral to process lifetime. Also: hardware page-fault storms when many lazy commits fire simultaneously. Rate-limit concurrent commits per-host and backpressure via tenant soft limit.

maria: rollout plan: 1) internal-only ALLOC_LAZY flag in staging (wrapper impl) 2) add ledger + TTL + GC + reserve metrics 3) add async_commit + hedging 4) canary on Dedicated (feature flag) + route-scoped opt-in 5) surface knobs in console and alerting.

raj: suggestion for canary: run two workloads side-by-side on dedicated-dev: heavy microbatch producer and steady-state long-lived model. Track fragmentation, avg token-cost, 99.9p latency. Feature toggle should include experiment id in telemetry.

deploy-bot: canary build queued: fe/alloc-lazy/wrap -> canary-dedicated-dev-42 :rocket:

maria: volunteers for first PR? @tomas for allocator wrapper, @alex for async commit, @jin for NUMA/offload tests. I'll own the RFC doc and telemetry.

alex: one more: compaction should treat aged reserved hints like small free holes and attempt coalescing. But be careful: aggressive compaction can increase tails if it forces commits. compactor policy: avoid compacting into space where live reserved_count > threshold.

lisa: agree. We'll add a compaction-safety window configured by reserved_timeout_ms.

maria: great. I'll circulate a short RFC patch with API sketch, state machine diagram (RESERVED_HINT -> COMMITTED -> PINNED), GC TTLs, hedging modes, and canary plan. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
